descripcion_es: Routines and general facts; third-person -s; do/does.
resumen: The present simple expresses habits, routines, likes and facts that are always true. In the third person singular the verb adds -s, and questions and negatives are formed with do or does.

explicacion.texto: It is used for things we do regularly (I work from nine to five), for likes and opinions (She likes jazz) and for general facts (Water boils at 100 degrees). It often goes with adverbs of frequency: always, usually, often, sometimes, never.

filas: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Yes, she does. / No, she doesn't.

items: Spelling of the -s: most verbs add -s (works); after -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -o add -es (watches, goes); consonant + y changes to -ies (studies).
With does and doesn't the verb goes back to the base form: Does he work? (not “Does he works?”).
Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb (I often walk) but after to be (I am often late).

ejemplos.frase: I get up at seven every day.
ejemplos.traduccion: Me levanto a las siete todos los días.

ejemplos.frase: He usually watches the news after dinner.
ejemplos.traduccion: Normalmente ve las noticias después de cenar.
La tienda abre a las nueve.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: In the third person singular the verb takes -s.
With does the verb is in the base form: the -s is already in does.
The negative is formed with don't or doesn't, not with no.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the verb in the present simple.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the central rule of the card: in the third person singular (he, she, it or an equivalent subject) the verb adds -s. My father is equivalent to he, so work becomes works. The sentence describes a regular, stable situation, so it is in the present simple and not the continuous.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mi padre trabaja en un hospital.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The third-person -s is missing: my father is equivalent to he and needs works.
The continuous would suggest something temporary; for his regular job, use works.
Work only adds -s; the ending -es is for verbs ending in -s, -sh, -ch, -x or -o.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the verb in the present simple.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains the spelling of the -s: verbs ending in -s, -sh, -ch, -x or -o add -es. Watch ends in -ch, so it becomes watches. The clue for the tense is every evening, which shows a habit, and the subject she requires the third-person form.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ella ve la tele todas las noches.

errores_previstos.explicacion: After -ch add -es, not just -s: watches.
The third-person ending is missing: she watches.
Every evening shows a habit: present simple, watches.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the verb in the present simple.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is another spelling rule in the card: when the verb ends in consonant + y, the y becomes -ies in the third person. Study ends in d + y, so it becomes studies. If the y came after a vowel (play), you would just add -s: plays. The subject Tom is equivalent to he and the sentence expresses a habit.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tom estudia inglés por la noche.

errores_previstos.explicacion: With consonant + y, the y changes to -ies: studies.
The third-person ending is missing: Tom studies.
The y does not stay: it becomes i and you add -es, studies.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with do, does, don't or doesn't.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card shows that present simple questions are formed with do or does + subject + base form of the verb. Do is used with I, you, we, they; does with he, she, it. The subject your children is plural and equivalent to they, so it takes Do. It is an affirmative question, so don't is not used.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Your children is equivalent to they: the question takes do.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¿A tus hijos les gustan las verduras?

errores_previstos.explicacion: Your children is plural (they): the question takes do, not does.
Like is a main verb, not be: the question is formed with do.
The sentence is not negative and does not show surprise; Do is enough.

ejercicios.explicacion: According to the card, the third-person negative is formed with doesn't (does not) + base form of the verb. My cat is equivalent to it, so it takes doesn't, and like has no -s, because does already carries the third-person marker. The answer is doesn't like or does not like.
ejercicios.traduccion: A mi gato no le gusta el agua.

errores_previstos.explicacion: After doesn't the verb goes back to the base form: like, with no -s.
My cat is third person singular (it): doesn't like.
The negative needs the auxiliary: doesn't like.

ejercicios.frase: He ___ to the gym on Mondays.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card shows that verbs ending in -o add -es in the third person: go → goes. The time clue is on Mondays, which shows a routine, and the subject he requires the third-person form. So the answer is goes.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Go in the third person is goes.
ejercicios.traduccion: Él va al gimnasio los lunes.

por_opcion.go: Incorrect: it is missing the third-person -es; it would work with I, you, we or they.
por_opcion.goes: Correct: third person of go (it ends in -o, so it adds -es) for a weekly habit.
por_opcion.going: Incorrect: an -ing form without be does not form a tense, and a routine requires the present simple.

ejercicios.explicacion: The card stresses that, with does and doesn't, the verb goes back to the base form: Does he work? (not Does he works?). The clue is Does at the beginning, which already carries the third-person marker. So the verb stays as have, although in a statement we would say she has.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: After does, use the base form.

por_opcion.has: Incorrect: has is the third-person form, but after does the verb goes back to the base form: have.
por_opcion.having: Incorrect: the -ing form cannot go after does.

ejercicios.explicacion: According to the table in the card, with I, you, we and they the verb is in the base form, with no -s. The subject we requires live. The -s only appears with he, she, it. The option with are mixes the verb be with another verb, a common mistake among Spanish speakers who translate “estamos viviendo” or mix up structures.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With we the verb has no -s.
ejercicios.traduccion: Vivimos en el centro de la ciudad.

por_opcion.lives: Incorrect: lives is the third person singular form; with we there is no -s.
por_opcion.are live: Incorrect: be and a base-form verb are not combined; the present simple of live is simply we live.

ejercicios.enunciado: Turn the sentence into a question.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card shows that the question is formed with Does + subject + base form of the verb when the subject is he, she or it. She plays becomes Does she play: the -s of plays disappears because does now carries it. The rest of the sentence (the guitar) does not change.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Question with does and the base form of the verb.

errores_previstos.explicacion: After does the verb is in the base form: play, with no -s.
In modern English main verbs are not inverted: does is needed.
With she the auxiliary is does, not do.

ejercicios.explicacion: According to the table in the card, with I, you, we and they the negative is formed with don't (do not) + base form of the verb. They drink becomes They don't drink. Both the contraction and the full form do not, which is more formal or emphatic, are accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: With they the negative is don't + verb.

errores_previstos.explicacion: With they the auxiliary is don't; doesn't is only for he, she, it.
A calque of Spanish “no beben”: English needs the auxiliary, don't drink.
After don't the verb is in the base form, and with they it never takes -s.

respuestas: My brother does not eat fish.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that the third person singular negative uses doesn't. My brother is equivalent to he, so don't is incorrect and must be changed to doesn't (or does not). The verb eat stays in the base form. It is a very common mistake in speech, but it is not standard usage.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: My brother is third person: doesn't.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: with my brother (he) you need doesn't.
After doesn't the verb goes back to the base form: eat.
The auxiliary is missing: doesn't eat.

ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the rule in the card: with does the verb goes back to the base form. The auxiliary carries the third-person marker, so lives must become live. The question order (Where + does + she + verb) is correct; only the -s is wrong.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: After does the verb has no -s.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: after does the verb has no -s.
The auxiliary does is missing: in a direct question the statement word order is not enough.
With she the auxiliary is does, not do.

respuestas: I always have breakfast at eight
At eight I always have breakfast
ejercicios.explicacion: The card says that adverbs of frequency go before the main verb (I often walk). So always goes between I and have: I always have breakfast at eight. The time expression at eight can go at the end or, with some emphasis, at the beginning. Have breakfast means to eat the morning meal.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The adverb of frequency goes before the main verb.
ejercicios.traduccion: Siempre desayuno a las ocho. (También: A las ocho siempre desayuno.)

errores_previstos.respuesta: I have always breakfast at eight
errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque from Spanish: always goes before the main verb, not after it.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Always I have breakfast at eight
errores_previstos.explicacion: In a neutral sentence the adverb of frequency goes between the subject and the verb.

ejercicios.enunciado: Put the words in order to make a question.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card gives the order of questions with a question word: question word + do/does + subject + base form of the verb. With you, use do, so the result is Where do you work. You cannot leave out do, even though the Spanish question has no auxiliary.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The auxiliary do goes before the subject: Where do you work.
The question word always goes at the beginning of the question.

descripcion_larga_es: The present simple is the tense of habits, routines, likes and general truths. It looks simple, but it hides two traps for Spanish speakers: the third person singular -s, which is very easy to forget, and the auxiliary do/does in questions and negatives, which does not exist in Spanish. Mastering it is the basis for everything else.

contexto.que_es: It is the most basic form of the present in English: the verb in the base form (I work) or with -s in the third person singular (she works). Questions and negatives are built with the auxiliary do/does followed by the base form of the verb.
contexto.por_que_importa: It is the tense used to describe daily life, work, likes and general facts, so it appears in any presentation or talk. Forgetting the -s (he work) or combining does with -s (Does she works?) are very visible mistakes that reveal a low level. Also, using it instead of the continuous, or the other way round, can change the meaning of what you say.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: It is signalled by adverbs of frequency (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) and expressions such as every day, on Mondays, at night. It is also used with state verbs (know, like, want). Spanish speakers tend to forget the -s, to ask questions without do (Where you work?) and to put the adverb of frequency after the verb, as in Spanish.
